subject: Temporary credential exposure — notify + request for IR evidence
messages:
From: Alex Turley <alex.turley@brightline-systems.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: sec+redwood@brightline-systems.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Potential temporary credential exposure (support ticket 2399)

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Quick heads up from my side — we noticed a presigned S3 URL in a support ticket that was public for ~2 hours yesterday (ticket 2399). It looks like the URL contained short-lived credentials that would have allowed object GETs. We cannot confirm unauthorized downloads yet, but we saw anomalous HEAD requests from a handful of IPs during that window.

Can you please:
- Confirm whether this was generated by Redwood support tooling or a customer-side link.
- Share your incident response process and any evidence we can accept for SIG/CAIQ / SOC2 follow-up (sanitized logs, rotatation proof, timeline).

I attached a small sample of the access log we pulled (access-log-sample.csv) — redacted where necessary. We can join a quick 20m call if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex Turley
Security Engineer — Brightline Systems
alex.turley@brightline-systems.com

(attachment: access-log-sample.csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turley <alex.turley@brightline-systems.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential temporary credential exposure (support ticket 2399)

Alex — thanks for the flag and for the sample.

Immediate update: we are treating this as a potential credentials exposure. Karthik, can you confirm if the presigned URL was created from our support portal (or customer-side)? Neha, I'm looping you in to lead containment / evidence collection.

Alex, we'll share our IRP and a sanitized evidence packet for SIG/CAIQ review. I propose a 20 minute call today at 11:30 PT to align on scope and what you need for audit acceptance. If that works for you, please paste a calendar invite; otherwise we'll DM an alternate time.

Appreciate the quick notice — we'll prioritize.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential temporary credential exposure (support ticket 2399)

Following up with actions I'm starting now:
- Containment: rotating service tokens for presigned-url generation, revoking any active sessions tied to the support tool.
- Evidence collection: pulling API gateway + S3 access logs for 7/30m/24h windows, capture of support-tool event history, and a sanitized timeline.
- Artifacts I'll produce: redacted access logs, rotation proof (token change entries), and a short IRP excerpt that shows our playbook steps.

Attached: redwood_irp_v3.pdf (internal IRP excerpt) — this is the section we'll use for external evidence; it omits internal-only checklists.

Karthik — please collect the gateway and S3 logs and drop to the evidence folder; mark anything that correlates to ticket 2399. Marissa, I'll draft a brief postmortem once we have the logs.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Security Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_irp_v3.pdf)

From: Alex Turley <alex.turley@brightline-systems.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential temporary credential exposure (support ticket 2399)

Thanks Neha — that helps. We pulled a small support-ticket export (attached) that contains the exact text where the presigned URL appeared (support-ticket-2399.txt). There are three GET attempts from two IP ranges that look suspicious; we redacted headers but included timestamps.

We need sanitized logs that show:
- Token issuance record (who/what generated the presigned URL)
- Rotation timestamp for affected tokens
- Any object-level GETs during the window (sanitized paths are fine)

If you can provide a short timeline + artifacts we can accept for our audit (PDFs or signed docs), that would be ideal. If SOC2 artifact crosswalk is needed, include that too.

Alex
(attachment: support-ticket-2399.txt)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turley <alex.turley@brightline-systems.com>, sec+redwood@brightline-systems.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 14:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary — temporary presigned URL exposure (ticket 2399)

Alex / Brightline team — sending the post-incident summary and evidence we discussed. Below is the concise timeline and mitigation; attached is a sanitized evidence bundle.

Executive summary:
- Incident: Presigned S3 URL containing short-lived credentials was accidentally included in support ticket 2399 by an internal support engineer. The URL was public in the ticket for ~2 hours on 2026-09-07 21:04–23:05 UTC.
- Impact: Object read access only (no writes observed). We observed three unusual GETs tied to two IP ranges; no exfiltration of large data sets detected in the logs provided.
- Root cause: Manual copy/paste of a presigned URL into a support ticket during troubleshooting; lack of client-side redaction step in that support workflow.

Containment & remediation:
- Rotated presigned-token issuance keys and revoked active presigned tokens at 2026-09-07T23:10:00Z.
- Implemented immediate support workflow change: support UI now strips presigned URLs by default and warns on potential credential leakage.
- Added a 1-hour automated scan for presigned URL patterns in tickets.

Evidence provided:
- Sanitized access logs (S3 + gateway) showing request timestamps and anonymized object identifiers (attached).
- Token rotation audit showing revocation timestamp and issuance of new keys (attached).
- Short postmortem brief (postmortem-temp-creds-brief.txt).

Attachments: postmortem-temp-creds-brief.txt, access-log-sample.csv (full sanitized export), rotation-audit.csv

We believe this packet satisfies SIG/CAIQ evidence needs for the event; let us know if you require a signed attestation or a SOC2 crosswalk (we can map artifacts to control IDs). I'm also happy to take a short call to walk through artifacts.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(attachment: postmortem-temp-creds-brief.txt)

From: Elaine Ford <elaine.ford@brightline-systems.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident summary — temporary presigned URL exposure (ticket 2399)

Marissa / Neha — thank you for the fast turnaround and for the clear postmortem. We reviewed the artifacts and the sanitized logs; this should be sufficient for our SIG review. Two asks before we close the loop:
1) Can you provide a short SOC2 artifact crosswalk (control mapping) that shows which of these artifacts correspond to CC6.1 / CC7.2 controls?
2) Our procurement team would like an internal attestation doc for our records (simple signed letter confirming rotation and mitigations is OK).

Looping in procurement: Elaine Ford <elaine.ford@brightline-systems.com> — she will coordinate the attestation.

Best,
Elaine Ford
Senior Procurement Manager — Brightline Systems
elaine.ford@brightline-systems.com
